Find Afternoon Work.name: Find Afternoon Work
Find Afternoon Work.questStatement: Your academy mornings are busy; paid afternoon work can cover ordinary life in town.
Find Afternoon Work.mainObjective: Arrange a paid part-time job or trial shift that fits around required classes.
Find Afternoon Work.questDesignBrief: An optional personal student goal, with no deadline or academy mandate. After morning classes, follow an actual work lead or approach an appropriate employer. Daichi Kamado at The Golden Ladle offers kitchen preparation and cleanup; Noriko Hanesawa at Roseberry Inn offers room turnover and common-room work; Lucien Delorme at The Everlight Public Library can discuss shelving or qualified copying. Other established employers are valid. Confirm duties, hours, pay and a first shift with a willing employer. Do not invent a vacancy at every shop or demand guild membership. Ordinary half-day help commonly pays 8-12 marks for completed work; skilled work is separately quoted. The player can reject an unsuitable offer. Accepting the job completes this arrangement goal but is not a completed shift or wage payment. No automatic relationship gain, stats, registration or badge. The player can postpone or abandon this goal.

arrange_work.text: Agree duties, hours, pay and a first shift with a willing employer.

completionCondition.query: For Find Afternoon Work, the player and a willing actual employer have agreed a paid recurring part-time role or paid trial shift, including concrete duties, hours compatible with classes, pay and when the first shift begins. A notice, inquiry, intention, unaccepted offer, refused arrangement or another player taking the job is not enough. Completing a future shift or receiving wages is not required to finish this arrangement goal.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Remember the employer, duties, pay, schedule and first shift agreed in Find Afternoon Work. The arrangement goal is complete. Pay wages only when actual work earns them; this completion grants no cash, skill level, relationship points or membership. Do not automatically play through the shift.

Your First Spell.name: Your First Spell
Your First Spell.questStatement: A little magic can become something of your own. Try designing your first personal spell.
Your First Spell.mainObjective: Create and safely demonstrate one simple original spell using Spellcraft.
Your First Spell.questDesignBrief:
An optional beginner experiment, available independently of school enrollment. Let the player choose a useful purpose and a discipline they actually know: a small light, a shaped breeze, a precise arcane nudge or another modest working. These are examples, not prescribed spells. A noncaster can postpone it or seek basic instruction; this goal does not teach a discipline or demand that a martial character become a mage.
Use an actual Spellcraft check to design or substantially adapt the blueprint. Then resolve a safe test with its actual discipline, effects and costs. A simple experiment can take one short scene; failed attempts invite a small revision, not a mandatory multi-session research project. Require a real successful design and a repeatable supported result, not just a name, promise, teacher demonstration or preexisting ability. Let the player name the spell, or offer a few vivid names after its function is known.
Use the normal learned-ability workflow to record the personal technique when eligible. A real cooldown may delay its card without undoing an already successful experiment. Do not grant free levels, an extra ability point or an unrelated spell. A teacher may be an existing academy professor or another genuinely qualified person; enrollment and paid instruction follow their actual circumstances. This experiment is not a second compulsory first-day class. If the same design also genuinely satisfies an accepted academy project, acknowledge the work rather than demanding a duplicate invention; preserve that project's own acceptance and requirements.

completionCondition.query: Since accepting Your First Spell, the player actually develops a modest original or substantially redesigned spell in a discipline they know, succeeds at the required Spellcraft design check, and demonstrates a safe reproducible result through a real casting test. A copied existing spell, invented success, proposed name, failed design, teacher doing all the work, or merely obtaining a spellbook is false. A pending ability-card cooldown does not invalidate a genuinely completed experiment.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Conclude Your First Spell with the actual invented function, chosen name and successful test. Its native completion grants the configured experience once. Preserve the personal working for the normal ability workflow; do not issue a second reward, force a thesis or invent an unearned ability.
